name: Sunifiram
lead: Sunifiram (DM-235) is an experimental nootropic from a series of piperazine compounds made by Italian researchers; it is a structural simplification of unifiram (DM-232). In animal studies it showed antiamnesic effects at much lower doses than piracetam.[1][2] It has not been approved anywhere.
As of 2016, it had undergone no toxicology testing and no human trials,[1][3] and sources reviewed do not connect it to physical appearance.
infobox: Unapproved new drug in the US[1]

paras: The mechanism is unknown. Broad screening found no affinity for tested receptors and transporters up to 1 micromolar, and it did not potentiate AMPA receptors directly, though it blocked amnesia from an AMPA antagonist.[1][4] Later mouse and hippocampal work linked it to the NMDA receptor glycine site and CaMKII and PKC activation.[5][6]
No studies found. A 2016 review in the Journal of Enzyme Inhibition and Medicinal Chemistry discussed how the compounds reached online markets without human data.[3]
The compound is not patented and is sold online as a research chemical or nootropic.[3]

quick.overview:
Sunifiram is an experimental nootropic developed in Italy and sold online. It is a simplified analogue of unifiram.

No source links it to appearance.
quick.mechanism: Its mechanism is unknown; research points to NMDA glycine-site and kinase pathways.
quick.risks: No human trials or toxicology testing have been published; unapproved in the US.
